idiom_name: sqlx::types::Json<T> over a json/jsonb column (serde derives)
implementation_notes: In sqlx, serde derives on the entity plus a sqlx::types::Json<Entity> field deliver the whole pattern with no hand-written mapper: the wrapper encodes and decodes the JSON representation against Postgres json/jsonb, MySQL JSON or SQLite TEXT, and a newtype can carry #[sqlx(json)] where one is wanted. Diesel declares the same column as Jsonb in its table! macro, with ToSql/FromSql implemented for serde_json::Value under the serde_json feature. Because the codec is a derive, payload compatibility is the Rust type's compatibility - the read fails at decode time when the document no longer matches, so defaults and a version key belong in the type.
pitfalls: serde errors on missing fields and ignores unknown ones by default: a renamed field turns old rows into decode errors - keep #[serde(default)] and an explicit version key for evolution.

The query! macros need the type override (`details as "details: Json<Details>"`) or the JSON column is inferred as the wrong Rust type; the macro then checks that type against the live database schema.
JSON support is feature-gated per database in sqlx, so a missing feature fails at compile time rather than at runtime.
